metadata.scope: Primary literature, numerical benchmark data, expert elicitation, and task-specific research. Evidence types are kept distinct.
limitations: This is a documented research selection, not an exhaustive review of all scientific fields or all human history.

Evidence describes observations, evaluations, historical patterns or explicitly attributed expert opinions. Numerical capability and deployment horizons are authored scenario assumptions, not calibrated estimates from these publications.
Dates refer to initial public versions except specifically identified corrections and reports; abstracts and relevant methods/limitations were reviewed, not every experiment independently replicated.
No publication after the evidence cutoff is included. Historical benchmark results must not be presented as current frontier performance.

sources.title: Measuring AI Ability to Complete Long Software Tasks
sources.observation: Measures success on software tasks by the time humans take, and reports a historical increase in the task length at which agents achieve 50% success.
sources.limitation: A 50% benchmark success horizon is not reliable autonomous employment. The trend concerns software tasks; its continuation and external validity are uncertain.
sources.forecastUse: Supports the capability distinction or uncertainty; does not supply the site’s milestone year.

sources.title: Time Horizon 1.1
sources.observation: Updates the task suite and time-horizon estimates with more long tasks and revised evaluation methods.
sources.limitation: Suite composition, human time estimates, agent scaffolding and measurement uncertainty affect the estimates. No cross-domain robotic progress rate is established.
sources.forecastUse: Supports the capability distinction or uncertainty; does not supply the site’s milestone year.

sources.title: OSWorld: Benchmarking Multimodal Agents for Open-Ended Tasks in Real Computer Environments
sources.observation: Introduces 369 real computer tasks with execution-based evaluation. Original experiments expose difficulty with GUI grounding and operational knowledge.
sources.limitation: The paper’s original scores are historical baselines, not current model scores; desktop benchmarks do not cover every workplace exception.
sources.forecastUse: Supports the capability distinction or uncertainty; does not supply the site’s milestone year.

sources.title: WebArena: A Realistic Web Environment for Building Autonomous Agents
sources.observation: Evaluates agents completing realistic, functionally checked tasks in websites rather than only producing plausible text.
sources.limitation: Original benchmark results are historical. Simulated websites and bounded tasks do not establish full workflow reliability or deployment economics.
sources.forecastUse: Supports the capability distinction or uncertainty; does not supply the site’s milestone year.

sources.title: SWE-bench: Can Language Models Resolve Real-World GitHub Issues?
sources.observation: Uses real repository issues requiring code edits and testing, highlighting multi-file context and environment interaction.
sources.limitation: Repository issue resolution is narrower than the complete software occupation. Initial results must not be represented as current frontier performance.
sources.forecastUse: Supports the capability distinction or uncertainty; does not supply the site’s milestone year.

sources.title: τ-bench: A Benchmark for Tool-Agent-User Interaction in Real-World Domains
sources.observation: Combines simulated users, tools and domain rules. Repeated-trial evaluation distinguishes occasional task success from consistent success.
sources.limitation: Simulated user interactions and selected service domains are not universal reliability evidence.
sources.forecastUse: Supports the capability distinction or uncertainty; does not supply the site’s milestone year.

sources.title: Open X-Embodiment: Robotic Learning Datasets and RT-X Models
sources.observation: Studies pooled robot experience and transfer across different robot embodiments, addressing fragmentation of robot training data.
sources.limitation: Transfer in the studied datasets does not demonstrate arbitrary dexterity or unattended operation in every environment.
sources.forecastUse: Supports the capability distinction or uncertainty; does not supply the site’s milestone year.

sources.title: π0.5: a Vision-Language-Action Model with Open-World Generalization
sources.observation: Reports generalization of robot manipulation to unfamiliar homes using heterogeneous training sources, including selected long household workflows.
sources.limitation: The reported tasks and environments are bounded demonstrations, not evidence of universal robotic labor or commercial cost competitiveness.
sources.forecastUse: Supports the capability distinction or uncertainty; does not supply the site’s milestone year.

sources.title: Gemini Robotics: Bringing AI into the Physical World
sources.observation: Introduces robotics-focused vision-language-action and embodied reasoning models that translate multimodal reasoning into robot control.
sources.limitation: A model report’s tested capabilities do not validate every physical work task; real-world generalization and safety need deployment-specific evaluation.
sources.forecastUse: Supports the capability distinction or uncertainty; does not supply the site’s milestone year.

sources.title: Learning Fine-Grained Bimanual Manipulation with Low-Cost Hardware
sources.publisher: Zhao, Kumar, Levine and Finn / RSS
sources.observation: Demonstrates precise two-arm imitation learning with low-cost hardware and action chunking on selected manipulation tasks.
sources.limitation: Training demonstrations, known hardware and selected tasks constrain the evidence; this is not general manipulation without supervision.
sources.forecastUse: Supports the capability distinction or uncertainty; does not supply the site’s milestone year.

sources.title: Mobile ALOHA: Learning Bimanual Mobile Manipulation with Low-Cost Whole-Body Teleoperation
sources.observation: Combines mobile movement and bimanual manipulation, using teleoperation demonstrations and co-training for selected whole-body tasks.
sources.limitation: Per-task training and experimental settings limit transfer claims; capital cost, maintenance and autonomous recovery are separate questions.
sources.forecastUse: Supports the capability distinction or uncertainty; does not supply the site’s milestone year.

sources.title: DROID: A Large-Scale In-The-Wild Robot Manipulation Dataset
sources.observation: Provides diverse real-world manipulation data and documents the logistical, safety and labor challenges of collecting robot experience.
sources.limitation: More data and observed transfer do not imply that every environment or contact interaction has been solved.
sources.forecastUse: Supports the capability distinction or uncertainty; does not supply the site’s milestone year.

sources.title: BEHAVIOR-1K: A Human-Centered, Embodied AI Benchmark with 1,000 Everyday Activities and Realistic Simulation
sources.observation: Builds a benchmark of 1,000 everyday activities with realistic objects and physical interactions, exposing complex long-horizon embodied demands.
sources.limitation: Simulation and a task benchmark are research infrastructure; they are not a demonstration of 1,000 fully autonomous real-world jobs.
sources.forecastUse: Supports the capability distinction or uncertainty; does not supply the site’s milestone year.

sources.title: SOTOPIA: Interactive Evaluation for Social Intelligence in Language Agents
sources.observation: Evaluates goal-directed social interactions in simulated situations, revealing variation across social dimensions and difficult scenarios.
sources.limitation: Simulated role play cannot establish real-world care, acceptance, trust or sustained relationship competence.
sources.forecastUse: Supports the capability distinction or uncertainty; does not supply the site’s milestone year.

sources.title: Autonomous Dissection in Robotic Cholecystectomy
sources.publisher: Oh, Borgioli, Žefran, Valle and Giulianotti
sources.observation: Combines visual segmentation, grasping, tissue tension and dissection in an autonomous architecture evaluated on ex vivo porcine livers.
sources.limitation: Ex vivo experimental dissection is not a complete autonomous operation or evidence of clinical approval and safety across patients.
sources.forecastUse: Supports the capability distinction or uncertainty; does not supply the site’s milestone year.

sources.title: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework (AI RMF 1.0)
sources.publisher: National Institute of Standards and Technology
sources.observation: Defines a risk-management framework treating validity, reliability, safety and governance in the context of deployment.
sources.limitation: This voluntary framework is neither an automation prediction nor a guarantee that a system meets a specific regulatory requirement.
sources.forecastUse: Supports the capability distinction or uncertainty; does not supply the site’s milestone year.

sources.title: An autonomous laboratory for the accelerated synthesis of inorganic materials
sources.observation: Integrates robotic synthesis, computational materials data, machine learning and experiment selection into a bounded closed-loop laboratory.
sources.limitation: Read with the 2026 correction. Original novelty and success claims were revised; the system’s targets and equipment are domain-specific.
sources.forecastUse: Supports the capability distinction or uncertainty; does not supply the site’s milestone year.

sources.title: Author Correction: An autonomous laboratory for the accelerated synthesis of inorganic materials
sources.observation: Corrects material-identification and novelty claims; the updated paper reports 36 of 57 targets successfully synthesized.
sources.limitation: Novelty relative to a prediction platform is not necessarily novelty to science. This correction illustrates the need for independent validation.
sources.forecastUse: Supports the capability distinction or uncertainty; does not supply the site’s milestone year.

sources.title: Scaling deep learning for materials discovery
sources.observation: Uses graph neural networks and first-principles calculations to expand candidate stable crystal structures and study generalization in materials modeling.
sources.limitation: Predicted thermodynamic stability is not proof of synthesizability, application suitability, manufacturing feasibility or a date for a new invention.
sources.forecastUse: Supports the capability distinction or uncertainty; does not supply the site’s milestone year.

sources.title: Autonomous mobile robots for exploratory synthetic chemistry
sources.observation: Integrates mobile robots, synthesis and multiple analytical instruments into exploratory chemistry workflows with automated decisions.
sources.limitation: The decision rules and criteria were designed by domain experts for selected chemistry. This is not unrestricted scientific autonomy.
sources.forecastUse: Supports the capability distinction or uncertainty; does not supply the site’s milestone year.

sources.title: What work can robots do?
sources.observation: Constructs a robotics task-exposure index and separates capability in limited settings from cost competitiveness, preferences and regulation.
sources.limitation: Industry research relies in part on language-model task ratings and economic assumptions. Exposure or bounded capability is not full-job automation; its cost extrapolations are conditional.
sources.forecastUse: Supports the capability distinction or uncertainty; does not supply the site’s milestone year.

sources.title: Beyond AI Exposure: Which Tasks are Cost-Effective to Automate with Computer Vision?
sources.publisher: Svanberg et al. / MIT Initiative on the Digital Economy
sources.observation: Models technical requirements and the economic decision to deploy computer vision; scale and system costs change which exposed tasks are economical.
sources.limitation: This cost model concerns selected vision tasks at its study assumptions. It does not estimate all forms of AI, future hardware or full occupational replacement.
sources.forecastUse: Supports the capability distinction or uncertainty; does not supply the site’s milestone year.

sources.title: Artificial Intelligence and the Modern Productivity Paradox: A Clash of Expectations and Statistics
sources.observation: Explains how complementary innovation, intangible investment and organizational change can delay measured productivity effects of new technologies.
sources.limitation: The mechanism supports distinguishing capability from implementation. It does not imply a fixed delay for every occupation.
sources.forecastUse: Supports the capability distinction or uncertainty; does not supply the site’s milestone year.

sources.title: An Exploration of Technology Diffusion
sources.publisher: Comin and Hobijn / American Economic Review
sources.observation: Studies 15 technologies across 166 countries over two centuries and finds large variation in adoption lags, with faster adoption for newer technologies.
sources.limitation: Country-level historical adoption is not a direct measure of full-job automation. The sample’s average lag must not be applied as a universal forecast.
sources.forecastUse: Supports the capability distinction or uncertainty; does not supply the site’s milestone year.

sources.title: How predictable is technological progress?
sources.observation: Uses historical technology cost data and hindcasting to study probabilistic forecasts and how errors grow with the forecast horizon.
sources.limitation: Cost improvements for established technologies are not forecasts of first discovery or proof of a universal progress rate. Published in Research Policy in 2016.
sources.forecastUse: Supports the capability distinction or uncertainty; does not supply the site’s milestone year.

sources.title: Statistical Basis for Predicting Technological Progress
sources.publisher: Nagy, Farmer, Bui and Trancik / PLOS ONE
sources.observation: Compares empirical laws for technology unit costs using historical data and out-of-sample forecast errors across multiple technologies.
sources.limitation: Rates vary across technologies, forecast errors grow, and a single cost measure omits other performance dimensions. It does not date unspecified breakthroughs.
sources.forecastUse: Supports the capability distinction or uncertainty; does not supply the site’s milestone year.

sources.title: Are Ideas Getting Harder to Find?
sources.publisher: Bloom, Jones, Van Reenen and Webb / American Economic Review
sources.observation: Finds rising research effort and declining research productivity in multiple historical industries, products and firms.
sources.limitation: These historical findings challenge effortless exponential extrapolation but do not establish inevitable stagnation or predict the effect of future AI researchers.
sources.forecastUse: Supports the capability distinction or uncertainty; does not supply the site’s milestone year.

sources.title: Thousands of AI Authors on the Future of AI
sources.publisher: Grace et al. / Journal of Artificial Intelligence Research
sources.observation: Surveys 2,778 AI researchers. Aggregate answers distinguish machines outperforming humans on all tasks (50% by 2047) from all occupations becoming fully automatable (50% by 2116).
sources.limitation: These are subjective survey aggregates under different question framings, not calibrated forecasts or occupation-specific dates. Later journal version published in 2025.
sources.forecastUse: Supports the capability distinction or uncertainty; does not supply the site’s milestone year.

sources.title: Re-examining rates of lithium-ion battery technology improvement and cost decline
sources.publisher: Ziegler and Trancik / Energy & Environmental Science
sources.observation: Harmonizes historical battery price, production, research and performance data; estimated improvement rates depend on whether energy density is included in the service measure.
sources.limitation: Established battery cost and energy-density trends do not predict a new battery chemistry, robot reliability, or a universal date for embodied automation.
sources.forecastUse: Motivates separate hardware and economic assumptions and sensitivity to the chosen progress metric.

sources.title: Accurate structure prediction of biomolecular interactions with AlphaFold 3
sources.observation: Predicts structures of complexes containing proteins, nucleic acids, small molecules and other molecular entities, with benchmark improvements over specialized tools.
sources.limitation: Structure prediction is a bounded scientific capability. It does not establish experimental validation, safe therapies or complete autonomous biomedical research.
sources.forecastUse: Shows scientific sub-capabilities can improve substantially while downstream validation remains a separate requirement.

sources.title: Generative AI and jobs: A 2025 update
sources.observation: Updates occupational GenAI exposure using task-level information, expert input and AI assessments, distinguishing different exposure gradients.
sources.limitation: Exposure measures potential technological effects; it is not a forecast of full occupational automation or a date when a job disappears.
sources.forecastUse: Context for interpreting occupational task exposure only; it supplies none of the model’s numerical milestone parameters.

sources.title: Employment Projections Frequently Asked Questions
sources.observation: Explains national employment projections with a ten-year horizon and how technology can affect productivity, occupational staffing and demand.
sources.limitation: Employment projections and AI exposure categories are not full-automation dates. This source is an evolving FAQ; the listed date is the review date, not a claimed publication date.
sources.forecastUse: Context separating labor-demand projections from technical automation scenarios; no numerical milestone parameters are taken from this FAQ.

sources.title: Task-Completion Time Horizons of Frontier AI Models — official TH1.1 numerical results
sources.observation: Publishes per-model release dates, 50% and 80% software-task horizons, measurement bounds and frontier flags. The downloaded snapshot contains 26 observations across two task-suite versions.
sources.limitation: The dashboard is no longer actively maintained and warns that horizons above 16 hours cannot be measured reliably with this suite. Its tasks are bounded software, ML and cybersecurity problems; it does not publish 99% reliability horizons or occupation automation dates.
sources.forecastUse: Numerical source for the reproducible TH1.1 log2-horizon regression. Only comparable frontier observations within the stated measurement boundary are used in the primary fit.

sources.title: On the estimation and validity of AI time horizons—a statistical look at the METR plot
sources.observation: Reanalyzes 228 tasks and 26 models with spline and item-response approaches, finding nonlinearities between human task duration and AI difficulty and improved predictive scoring under alternative models.
sources.limitation: A statistical reanalysis of the measured task distribution does not directly forecast future capabilities or entire occupations. It is a preprint, and its alternatives do not remove external-validity uncertainty.
sources.forecastUse: Motivates explicit model-form uncertainty; an exponential trend fit to published horizons is useful as a conditional benchmark extrapolation rather than a universal progress law.

sources.title: 2023 Expert Survey on Progress in AI — cleaned responses and reproduced milestone distributions
sources.publisher: AI Impacts; Grace et al.; data repository by Tom Adamczewski
sources.type: primary survey dataset; independently derived distribution
sources.observation: The October 2023 survey elicited 10/50/90% years or probabilities at fixed horizons for 39 tasks, four named occupations, HLMI and FAOL. This project independently fits gamma CDFs and pools both framings to derive milestone belief quantiles.
sources.limitation: Expert beliefs are not calibrated capability measurements. Task feasibility and full occupations have different scopes. Derived fitting is not the exact original pipeline; FAOL median differs by about seven years from the published result. Tails and transfer to other tasks are especially uncertain.
sources.forecastUse: Provides dated, scope-specific conditional milestone anchors. Numerical transfer, integration, reliability and deployment adjustments remain separate modeling assumptions.

sources.title: SRT-H: A Hierarchical Framework for Autonomous Surgery via Language Conditioned Imitation Learning
sources.publisher: Kim et al. / Johns Hopkins / Stanford
sources.observation: Reports successful autonomous execution of evaluated cholecystectomy steps in all eight trials on unseen ex vivo gallbladders.
sources.limitation: Small ex vivo experiment on selected steps; it does not establish clinical complication rates, autonomous patient care or full surgeon automation.
sources.forecastUse: A bounded demonstrated surgical milestone; does not itself supply a future automation year.

sources.title: Task adaptation of Vision-Language-Action model: 1st Place Solution for the 2025 BEHAVIOR Challenge
sources.publisher: Larchenko, Zarin and Karnatak / Robot Learning Collective
sources.type: research paper and author results report
sources.observation: Winning 50-task household simulation policy reported private full-task success 0.124 and partial-progress q-score 0.260; demonstrations averaged 6.6 minutes.
sources.limitation: Simulation, task-specific training and inference corrections; a q-score is not the complete-task success rate, and neither establishes real-home deployment reliability.
sources.forecastUse: Separates partial progress from end-to-end success and supports coupled physical requirements; no calendar forecast is supplied.

sources.title: What work can robots do? — task-level research dataset
sources.type: published AI-assisted task assessments with cited examples
sources.observation: Contains 18,796 task classifications and 56,933 cited references. Physical execution is distinguished from human computer use. Capability tiers identify the setting in which cited robots are reported to perform example tasks.
sources.limitation: Ratings, task examples and time shares were generated with AI-assisted research. Exposure is not complete occupational automation; citations have not all been independently verified by AFTERMATH. This app does not treat generated time shares as measured data.
sources.forecastUse: Exact occupation-code, task-ID and statement joins add task-specific physical/nonphysical assessments and source links. No exposure tier is directly converted into an automation year.
